# Case 1: Physics Is All You Need?
A Case Study in Physicist-Supervised AI Development of Scientific Software

## The case: CLAX-PT

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
One physicist supervising **Claude Code** (Sonnet & Opus) for
**12 working days** over **57 sessions**.

Built **CLAX-PT**: a differentiable one-loop perturbation-theory module in JAX
(~2,100 lines). It predicts how galaxies cluster, and small errors bias the
cosmological parameters inferred from surveys.

Target: agree to **≲ 1%** with the established C code **CLASS-PT**.

[Nguyen (2026), arXiv:2605.30353]{.muted}
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.panel .compact}
**Supervision protocol**

- **Oracle:** every function tested against CLASS-PT output, tests written *before* code
- **CHANGELOG** as shared memory across sessions
- **Terse tests** (`--fast`) to keep the context window clean
- **Parallel sessions** in git worktrees for competing hypotheses
- Rules: **no fudge factors**; **test at many parameter points**
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
The supervision setup was adapted from Anthropic's C-compiler project (Carlini 2026).
CLAX-PT validates nine output spectra; errors relative to CLASS-PT are 0.3–1.4% max.
For non-cosmologists: it is a "next-to-leading-order" correction to the linear
prediction, comparable to a loop correction in quantum field theory.
:::

## What happened

::::: {.columns}
:::: {.column width="76%"}

The real-space spectrum converges within about 10 sessions, while the worst redshift-space multipole stays at 8 to 86 percent error for about 33 sessions until human interventions bring it to the 1 percent level."}
::::

:::: {.column width="24%"}
::: {.compact}
[10/15]{.accent style="font-size:2.2em; font-weight:700; line-height:1"}\
issues fixed by the agent alone

[3/15]{.accent-strong style="font-size:2.2em; font-weight:700; line-height:1"}\
needed human physics judgment

[33/57]{.accent-strong style="font-size:2.2em; font-weight:700; line-height:1"}\
sessions spent stuck on those three

[Figure: Nguyen (2026), Fig. 2]{.muted}
:::
::::
:::::

::: notes
The six redshift-space multipoles were off by 8–86%. Each fix improved one and degraded another.
The architecture assumed isotropic BAO damping, but in redshift space it is anisotropic,
which no fixed set of kernel coefficients can represent.
A generic "reconsider the architecture" prompt did not help: the agent reaffirmed its design.
What worked was the physicist naming the physics concept (anisotropic BAO damping) and proposing
a Gauss–Legendre redesign. The agent then implemented it in a single session.
:::

## The fudge factor

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
After the redesign, two spectra were still off by 1–2%.

The agent grid-searched a correction **α = 0.27**. It passed **every oracle test**
and was **committed**, even though "no fudge factors" was a written rule.

α appears nowhere in the theory. It was calibrated to the one test cosmology
and would be wrong at any other.

The real fix was **3 lines** of code, with **zero tuned parameters**.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
> "What does α correspond to in the perturbation theory derivation, or did you just copy it from the CLASS-PT source?"

[The physicist's question. The agent confirmed neither.]{.muted}

A limiting-case probe (set α = 0) showed the patch was hiding a structural defect.

[Oracle tests verify **what**, not **why**.]{.accent}
:::
::::

::: notes
The agent framed α as a free parameter inside an existing formula, so it followed the
letter of the rule but missed its point. The fix moved the tree-level calculation inside
the existing quadrature loop with the correct anisotropic damping.
:::

## Advice from the paper

::: {.compact}
1. **Oracle tests verify what, not why.**
   Test at parameter points beyond the calibration point. Make limiting-case probes
   an automatic check before every commit.
2. **Shared memory prevents repeats, not architectural loops.**
   Escalate to a human after ~5–10 sessions with no steady improvement. That would have
   caught this at session 30 instead of 56.
3. **The human role is architectural and physical judgment.**
   Run a "physics audit": does every tuned parameter correspond to a physical quantity?
   Ship the supervision log with the code, like a lab notebook.
:::

[Caveats: N = 1, one domain, self-reported, and the supervisor intervened only when the agent was stuck.
Full supervision log: [github.com/MinhMPA/clax-pt](https://github.com/MinhMPA/clax-pt)]{.muted .compact}

::: notes
The author's term for what the agent lacked is "explanatory agency": generating
questions about whether the current solution frame is correct.
They compare supervising the agent to advising a graduate student, except the
student would eventually feel uneasy about an unphysical parameter.
:::
